exposure: Increased fetal movement (defined as a fetal movement parameter above the 90th percentile)
cohort: 471 pregnant women who recorded fetal movement weekly at night using a fetal movement acceleration measurement recorder after 28 weeks gestation.
finding: Increased long-term gross fetal movement has a protective effect against preterm birth, non-cephalic presentation at birth, and Cesarean delivery.
mod_finding: Increased fetal movement was associated with a lower rate of Cesarean deliveries.
